blocks.text: Obfy renames and hardens your compiled .NET assemblies before you ship them, so the shipped build is harder for others to reverse-engineer. The app writes protected copies and will not write over an input file: a run whose output would replace one does not start, and the run bar says why. With one file and no output folder, the copy is named `MyApp.obfuscated.dll` and sits next to the original.
Start on Files. Drop assemblies, a solution or a project onto the window, or choose **Add files**. **Standard** protection is selected for you and is a good first run.

Press **Obfuscate** or {Ctrl+Enter}. The bar at the bottom says what the run will do, and why it cannot start when it cannot. When every file succeeds, Results opens with a summary and the symbols. If a file fails, you stay where you are: open Results and read the Log tab. On Results, **Preview** shows nothing until you choose an output assembly.

To read a stack trace from the protected build later, turn on **Write a symbol map** on Files before the run, because it is off by default. Or choose **Export symbol map…** on Results right after the run. Results are not kept after the next run or after you close the app.
Always run your own tests against the protected build before you ship it, and test the exact files you ship.

blocks.title: Obfuscation is not confidentiality
blocks.text: String, constant, resource and method body encryption, and native packing, hide values from casual inspection. The key is stored in the output, so anyone who runs or inspects it can recover the content: XOR trivially, AES-256 with a little more effort. Do not ship real secrets such as keys, tokens or credentials in an assembly and rely on obfuscation.
Most of these work wherever the window has focus. Where one does not, its row says so.

items.label: Save configuration
items.note: Saves to the file you opened or last saved. Asks where the first time.

items.label: Run
items.note: Only while no run is going, and when the run bar says the run can start.

items.label: Remove selected files
items.note: Click a row in the file list first. Not during a run.

blocks.text: {Ctrl+C} copies selected text, as in any page. To copy log lines, use **Copy** on the Log tab: it copies the lines you can see.
